--- title: "Day 1 — Spatial Data Retrieval & Analysis" subtitle: "From APIs to clean, analysis-ready datasets in R" author: "Your Name" format: revealjs bibliography: references.bib --- ## Setup ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(sf) library(terra) library(rgbif) library(CoordinateCleaner) library(rnaturalearth) library(tidyverse) library(ggspatial) theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 13)) ``` ::: ## Spatial Data: A Primer {background-color="#003366" .white-text} ## What is Spatial Data? > Data that explicitly represents **location** on Earth's surface, > using coordinates within a defined **reference system**. :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ### Vector (`sf`) - Points → occurrences - Lines → rivers, roads - Polygons → protected areas ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ### Raster (`terra`) - Continuous gridded surfaces - Elevation, temperature, NDVI - Each cell = one value ::: :::: ::: aside Comprehensive treatment in @lovelace2019geocomputation and @pebesma2023spatial. ::: ## Coordinate Reference Systems The mathematical framework that links coordinates to locations on Earth. $$ \text{CRS} = \{\,\text{datum},\ \text{projection},\ \text{units}\,\} $$ ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Always declare CRS explicitly with EPSG codes st_crs(4326) # WGS 84 — geographic, degrees st_crs(3857) # Web Mercator — projected, metres st_crs(2100) # GGRS87 / Greek Grid — projected, metres ``` ::: ::: {.callout-important} ## Always check the CRS Mismatched CRS is the **#1 source of errors** in spatial analysis. ::: ## The `sf` Workflow ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Read country boundary greece <- ne_countries(country = "Greece", scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf") # Inspect greece |> st_geometry() |> plot() # Reproject greece_2100 <- st_transform(greece, 2100) # Compute area greece_2100 |> st_area() |> units::set_units("km^2") ``` ::: ## The `terra` Workflow ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(terra) library(geodata) # Download WorldClim bioclimatic variables (10 arc-min) bioclim <- worldclim_global(var = "bio", res = 10, path = "data/raw") # Crop to Greece extent greece_ext <- ext(19, 30, 34, 42) bio_gr <- crop(bioclim, greece_ext) # Plot annual mean temperature (BIO1) plot(bio_gr[[1]], main = "Annual Mean Temperature (°C)") ``` ::: ## Retrieving GBIF Occurrences {background-color="#003366" .white-text} ## `rgbif`: Programmatic Access to GBIF ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(rgbif) # 1. Resolve a taxon key key <- name_backbone(name = "Quercus ilex")$usageKey # 2. Search occurrences in Greece with valid coordinates occ <- occ_search( taxonKey = key, country = "GR", hasCoordinate = TRUE, hasGeospatialIssue = FALSE, limit = 5000 ) # 3. Extract and convert to sf pts <- occ$data |> select(species, decimalLongitude, decimalLatitude, year, basisOfRecord, datasetKey) |> drop_na(decimalLongitude, decimalLatitude) |> st_as_sf(coords = c("decimalLongitude", "decimalLatitude"), crs = 4326) ``` ::: ## Visualising Raw Occurrences ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot() + annotation_map_tile(type = "cartolight", zoom = 6) + geom_sf(data = greece, fill = NA, color = "grey30") + geom_sf(data = pts, color = "#4A7C59", alpha = 0.5, size = 1) + labs(title = expression(italic("Quercus ilex") ~ "occurrences in Greece"), subtitle = "Source: GBIF.org", caption = "CRS: EPSG:4326") + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")) ``` ::: ## Data Cleaning Pipeline ```{mermaid} flowchart LR A[Raw GBIF
records] --> B[Remove
duplicates] B --> C[Flag
centroids & 0,0] C --> D[Spatial
thinning] D --> E[Validate
taxonomy] E --> F[(Analysis-ready
dataset)] style A fill:#B22234,color:white style F fill:#4A7C59,color:white ``` ## Cleaning with `CoordinateCleaner` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(CoordinateCleaner) flags <- clean_coordinates( x = as.data.frame(occ$data), lon = "decimalLongitude", lat = "decimalLatitude", species = "species", tests = c("capitals", "centroids", "equal", "gbif", "institutions", "zeros", "seas") ) # Keep only records that pass all tests clean <- occ$data[flags$.summary, ] ``` ::: ::: {.callout-tip} `clean_coordinates()` returns a logical matrix flagging each test individually — inspect failures **before** discarding! ::: ## Spatial Thinning to Reduce Sampling Bias ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Thin to one record per ~5 km grid cell thin_grid <- function(pts, cell_km = 5) { pts |> st_transform(2100) |> mutate(cell = paste( floor(st_coordinates(geometry)[, 1] / (cell_km * 1000)), floor(st_coordinates(geometry)[, 2] / (cell_km * 1000)))) |> group_by(cell) |> slice(1) |> ungroup() |> st_transform(4326) } pts_thin <- thin_grid(pts, cell_km = 5) ``` ::: ## Quality Control: Before vs After ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(patchwork) p1 <- ggplot(greece) + geom_sf(fill = "grey95") + geom_sf(data = pts, color = "#B22234", alpha = 0.4, size = 0.8) + labs(title = paste("Raw —", nrow(pts), "records")) + theme_void() p2 <- ggplot(greece) + geom_sf(fill = "grey95") + geom_sf(data = pts_thin, color = "#4A7C59", alpha = 0.6, size = 0.8) + labs(title = paste("Thinned —", nrow(pts_thin), "records")) + theme_void() p1 + p2 ``` ::: ## Hands-on Exercise 1 {background-color="#003366" .white-text} ### 🛠️ Your turn (45 min) 1. Pick a Mediterranean species (plant or animal) 2. Retrieve GBIF occurrences with `rgbif::occ_search()` 3. Apply `CoordinateCleaner::clean_coordinates()` 4. Map raw vs cleaned distribution side-by-side 5. Briefly discuss flagged records with your neighbour ⏱️ We reconvene at **14:15** ## Take-aways from Day 1 - The R spatial stack (`sf` + `terra`) covers the full data pipeline - Always verify and harmonise **CRS** before any spatial operation - GBIF data are powerful but **noisy** — clean systematically - Document every step → **reproducibility is non-negotiable** ::: {.callout-note} Tomorrow we move from *where* species occur to *how diverse* assemblages are. ::: ## References ::: {#refs} :::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
